topic_description: graph clustered federated learning for non-IID graph classification using dynamic time warping

Graph-Aware Dynamic Time Warping for Fed.Problem: Existing federated learning approaches for graph classification struggle with non-IID graph data across clients, especially when the graph structures and temporal dynamics vary significantly.
Graph-Aware Dynamic Time Warping for Fed.Existing Methods: Current methods typically use graph neural networks (GNNs) with federated averaging, but fail to capture complex temporal dependencies in dynamic graphs.
Graph-Aware Dynamic Time Warping for Fed.Motivation: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) has shown promise in aligning temporal sequences, but has not been effectively integrated into federated graph learning frameworks. Combining DTW with graph-aware federated learning could better handle non-IID graph data with varying temporal dynamics.
Graph-Aware Dynamic Time Warping for Fed.Proposed Method: We propose Graph-DTW-Fed, a novel federated learning framework for non-IID graph classification. The key ideas are: 1) A graph-aware DTW layer that aligns temporal graph sequences across clients before aggregation. 2) A hierarchical attention mechanism that learns to focus on important nodes, edges, and time steps when performing DTW. 3) A federated optimization strategy that alternates between local graph DTW updates and global model aggregation. 4) A clustering module that groups clients with similar graph dynamics to enable more effective knowledge transfer. The local models use graph neural networks augmented with our graph-DTW layers. During training, clients perform local updates using their private graph data. The server then clusters clients and performs aggregation within each cluster using our hierarchical attention mechanism. This process is repeated for multiple rounds to obtain a global model that can generalize across diverse graph distributions.
Graph-Aware Dynamic Time Warping for Fed.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate on multiple dynamic graph classification benchmarks like DYNGRAPH2VEC and JODIE, comparing against federated GNN baselines. Key metrics include classification accuracy, F1 score, and communication efficiency. We will also analyze how performance varies with graph structural differences and temporal misalignment between clients.

Multi-View Contrastive Federated Graph L.Problem: Existing federated graph learning methods struggle to learn robust representations for non-IID graph data, especially when graph views and structures differ significantly across clients.
Multi-View Contrastive Federated Graph L.Existing Methods: Current approaches typically use graph neural networks with federated averaging, but fail to leverage multiple complementary views of graphs that may be available.
Multi-View Contrastive Federated Graph L.Motivation: Contrastive learning has shown great promise in learning robust representations from multiple views of data. Integrating multi-view contrastive learning into federated graph classification could help overcome non-IID challenges.
Multi-View Contrastive Federated Graph L.Proposed Method: We propose FedMVCG (Federated Multi-View Contrastive Graph learning), a novel framework for non-IID graph classification. Key components include: 1) A multi-view graph encoder that learns from different structural and attribute-based views of each graph. 2) A federated contrastive loss that aligns representations across clients without sharing raw data. 3) An adaptive view importance learning module that determines optimal view combinations for each client. 4) A graph diffusion augmentation technique to generate additional views. 5) A personalization layer that adapts the global model to each client's distribution. During training, each client generates multiple views of their local graphs using random walk, subgraph sampling, and attribute masking. The multi-view encoder processes these to produce graph embeddings. The federated contrastive loss encourages consistency between views within and across clients. The server aggregates and updates view importance weights. Clients then fine-tune the personalization layer on local data. This process iterates to learn a robust global model that can generalize across heterogeneous graph distributions.
Multi-View Contrastive Federated Graph L.Experiment Plan: We will evaluate on diverse graph classification datasets like PROTEINS, COLLAB, and REDDIT-BINARY under non-IID splits. Baselines include federated GNNs and centralized multi-view graph learning methods. We'll measure classification accuracy, AUC-ROC, and representation quality via downstream tasks. We'll also analyze how performance varies with the degree of distribution shift between clients.
